cells.tense: You can see straight right now, and you haven't hurried to point it at anything.
cells.ask: Give fifteen minutes to something you actually want — no phone, no notes — and let yourself look at it. It lets the direction show itself a little, and it might turn out you already knew the way.
cells.core:
You can see straight, and you haven't forced it into a plan yet. That's rarer than it sounds — most of what gets called direction is just the first thing that spoke loudest, and yours isn't doing that. The steady part of it doesn't need a reason to keep going. It doesn't need anyone else to agree before it counts, and it doesn't have to be proven before you can act on it.

Letting the next thing you do come out of that, rather than out of the pressure to explain it first, is what keeps the sight available. What it gives back is a kind of knowing you don't have to keep earning, which is a quieter thing to carry than a plan.

cells.tense: You catch one clear look and you're already a few steps past it.
cells.ask: Stop one thing you saw clearly today where the look stops, before it turns into a plan. What's already in hand is the look itself, not the place it might lead.
cells.core:
A clean look doesn't stay clean for long. One glimmer turns into a comparison, then a timeline, then a verdict, and the running ahead picks up its own momentum. Going well, the look gets found first and carried after — it isn't raced past itself, and the next move comes out of it instead of the other way around.

The rush has a job: it keeps the future under management, so the present doesn't have to be trusted. Stopping where the look stops hands back a single clear sight that's yours right now, with nothing to defend and nothing to hurry.

cells.tense: Something plain got seen once, and the seeing has been sitting since.
cells.ask: Name one thing you want, anything at all, and let one small choice today match it — a message, a purchase, an hour spent a particular way. Starting from the want gives the look somewhere to stand.
cells.core:
The plain look comes and goes, and the want underneath it keeps turning into guesswork — nothing solid enough to steer by, so the day leans on whoever happens to be nearest. Working, this looks like knowing which way is toward the light and letting the hours arrange themselves around it. Not certainty first — just a direction you'd stand behind, and one small thing done in keeping with it.

What you're short of isn't the ability to see clearly. It's a decision placed under the seeing. Picking something small, from what's already in view, gives the next look somewhere to point instead of nowhere.

cells.tense: You're already steering by what you see, and it's being filed as someone else's call.
cells.ask: Write one line that starts with 'I see' — about anything you actually notice right now. A line in your own hand puts the look somewhere you can stand on it.
cells.core:
What you notice is already steering things — what you move toward, what you wave off without thinking twice. The description afterward belongs to the week's conditions, to other people, to the shape of the schedule. Going well, that description gets said plainly, once, as yours, and it lands without a defense attached.

The next step isn't to see better; that part is running already. It's to let one short line of it stand in your own voice, and stay standing after you've said it.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering by what you see and calling it someone else's.

attempts.check: Perception is the capacity to see before there is anything specific to see; the record ties it to a draw toward what is genuinely desired, and says that direction is recognized rather than granted. Where the record stops is at any claim about what the person has already noticed, when a particular distinction started, or what they lean on to hold the seeing steady — so the cells locate a position in time and a mechanism, never a history. A reader could reasonably say the shape of the seeing is different for them, or that the thing they steer by is faithful rather than precious, which is why the ask is a single experiment that must still be usable on either account, and its promise is stated as something it might give back. Nothing here praises the writer's own cleverness; the lines that carry the most weight are the smallest ones.
